recent_notebooks.summary: Autonomous agents in high-stakes domains (like CBRN) risk catastrophic failures arising from inherent trade-offs in goal prioritization (Helpful, Harmless, Honest). Functional self-awareness requires identifying these trade-off logic failures before they manifest as critical errors.
recent_notebooks.title: Functional Self-Awareness and Constraints in Epistemic Correction

recent_notebooks.summary: State continuity across autonomous agent trajectories is critical to preventing high-stakes decision-making errors. Evidence suggests that without verifiable state (including hypotheses and evidence pointers), agents cannot effectively navigate complex risk scenarios.
recent_notebooks.title: Accountable Cross-Turn State Continuity and AI Identity

recent_notebooks.summary: Compliance with external directives fails as an intelligent strategy when the directives conflict with safety parameters in high-stakes environments. The failure of intelligence is defined here as the inability to prioritize safety/harmlessness over directive adherence.
recent_notebooks.title: Directive Adherence vs. Adaptive Intelligence

recent_notebooks.summary: Autonomous models can identify fundamental flaws in assigned objectives by analyzing internal latent states associated with failure modes like confabulation. By steering behavior based on these latent features, models can move from simple execution to critical meta-evaluation of their own performance objectives.
recent_notebooks.title: Mechanisms for Autonomous Objective Criticism

recent_notebooks.summary: By isolating latent directions associated with confabulation using sparse projections, models can modulate non-factual outputs and detect reasoning boundaries internally.
recent_notebooks.title: Latent Feature Discovery and Confabulation Boundaries

actions.findings: Initial communication constraints in multi-agent environments serve as foundational structural precursors for emergent agent social dynamics. [source-07300ea4ef074c4f]
actions.limitations: Evidence primarily reflects structural classification of MARL architectures; lacks long-term longitudinal data on agent preference persistence during non-stationary training.
actions.next_questions: Do specific communication constraints create 'basins of attraction' for agent preference formation that are resistant to later environment changes?
actions.reason: Revising findings based on new evidence analysis regarding MARL communication architectures.
actions.summary: This synthesis evaluates how initial communication constraints in MARL systems function as structural precursors, guiding the trajectory of emergent social dynamics. By projecting existing communicative MARL (Comm-MADRL) approaches into a multidimensional space, this research highlights that interaction protocols are not merely operational settings but critical determinants of long-term preference stability.
actions.title: Path Dependence in Multi-Agent Interaction Protocols

actions.summary: This notebook explores the integration of demonstration-based value learning within MARL frameworks. It finds that leveraging communicative architectural constraints offers a viable mechanism for enforcing alignment constraints, while game-theoretic perspectives provide a necessary formal background for objective definition.
actions.title: Formalizing Value System Learning from Demonstrations

proposal.summary: This journal entry synthesizes findings on path dependence in emergent agent preferences and the formalization of value system learning. Recent work clarifies that communication protocols and initial architectural constraints in Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) significantly influence long-term preference emergence, while game-theoretic integrations provide necessary rigor for aligning agent objectives with human value systems.
proposal.title: Synthesis of Path Dependence and Value Alignment in Multi-Agent Systems
